transcript.speaker: Clarity
transcript.dialogue: Flatland, by Edwin Abbott Abbott, begins with a world confined to a plane  From above, we can see triangles and squares.

transcript.speaker: Clarity
transcript.dialogue: The first half of the book is also a social satire  Shapes mark status.

transcript.speaker: Clarity
transcript.dialogue: In a dream, the Square visits Lineland  Its king knows only one dimension and cannot understand a second.

transcript.speaker: Clarity
transcript.dialogue: Now move the sphere through the plane  Before contact, there is no intersection.

transcript.speaker: Clarity
transcript.dialogue: The Sphere eventually lifts the Square outside his world  A new viewpoint makes previously hidden interiors visible.

transcript.speaker: Clarity
transcript.dialogue: The return to Flatland brings resistance, not celebration  The Square struggles to explain his discovery and is punished for it.
